conflicts: 8s 2S1/2 energy: NIST / Sansonetti Table 5 give 19739.98(3) cm^-1 for 212Fr (level reference: Biemont et al. 1998 compilation with Ritz-formula predictions); the direct two-photon measurements give 19732.52411(15) cm^-1 for 210Fr and 19732.41-19732.59 cm^-1 for 208-213Fr (Kalita et al. 2018; Simsarian et al. 1999: 19732.523(4)). The 7.5 cm^-1 difference is far larger than any isotope shift (0.1 cm^-1), so the NIST 8s value, and every NIST wavelength involving 8s, appears to be off by about 7.5 cm^-1.

9p and 10p energies: NIST 27118.21 / 27366.20 / 29064.18 / 29198.09 cm^-1 are semi-empirical (Ritz formula, Biemont et al.); first measurements (221Fr, Lassegues et al. 2026) give 27111.238(5) / 27360.097(5) / 29058.1(6)[8] / 29192.8(8)[8] cm^-1, i.e. 5-7 cm^-1 lower (221Fr - 212Fr isotope shifts are below 1 cm^-1).
7d energies: NIST 24244.03 / 24332.93 cm^-1 (212Fr, Biemont compilation) against measured 24244.831(3) / 24333.298(3) cm^-1 in 210Fr (Grossman et al. 2000, Sansonetti Table 7): 0.8 and 0.4 cm^-1.

6d energies (16229.87, 16429.64 cm^-1): carried by NIST with the Biemont et al. reference; no direct measurement was found (Lassegues et al. 2026 list 6d as ongoing work), so the 7p-6d wavelengths are predictions.

8p 2P1/2 lifetime: measured 149.3(35) ns (210Fr, Aubin et al. 2004) against all-order theory 129.4(98) ns on the UDel portal (2 sigma); 8p 2P3/2: 83.5(15) ns (210Fr) and 81.1(17) ns (221Fr, 2026) against theory 77.8(42) ns.
D1 isotope shift 212Fr - 221Fr: 22437(4) MHz (Collister et al. 2014, MOT) against 22452(1) MHz printed in Sansonetti 2007 Table 2.
A(7p 2P1/2) of 212Fr: Sansonetti 2007 prints 1187(7) MHz (Duong et al. 1987); Grossman et al. 1999 measured 1192.0(2) MHz (entry); Collister et al. 2014 Table I lists 1192.2(1) MHz.

D2 isotope-shift uncertainties: Sansonetti 2007 Table 2 prints -23 570.0(2), -1 641.0(2), -20 806.8(5) MHz for 221, 213, 220 relative to 212, while Collister et al. 2014 quote the same Duong et al. shift as 23570(2) MHz; the 2 MHz uncertainty was adopted for 221 and 213.
10p 2P3/2 lifetime: Table I of Lassegues et al. prints 362(5)[3] ns, their supplement Table IV 362(7)[3] ns.

9s 2S1/2 lifetime attribution: 107.53(90) ns is attributed to Aubin et al., Opt. Lett. 28, 2055 (2003) by Lassegues et al. and to Aubin et al., Phys. Rev. A 70, 042504 (2004) by Sansonetti; same number.

A(9s 2S1/2) of 210Fr: Allegrini et al. 2022 note an inconsistency inside Gomez et al. 2008 between its Table 1 and its text; 622.25(36) MHz (text/abstract, also on the UDel portal) is the checked value.
B(7p 2P3/2) of 220Fr: +126.8(5) MHz in Allegrini et al. 2022 but -126.8(5) MHz in Sansonetti 2007 Table 2; 220Fr was left out of the hyperfine block.

7s - 8p rates: NIST ASD (Biemont et al. 1998, semi-empirical) lists A = 2.82e6 s^-1 (8p 2P3/2) and 2.64e6 s^-1 (8p 2P1/2), i.e. matrix elements 0.648 and 0.459 e a0 on the site; the UDel all-order values are 5.82(62)e6 and 1.34(27)e6 s^-1 (0.932(50) and 0.328(33) e a0). The NIST Fr I rates in general are semi-empirical and differ from the all-order values by up to a factor 2 for weak lines.

notes: NIST level energies refer to 212Fr (Sansonetti 2007 Table 5); several of them (6d, 8s, 7d, 9s, 9p-12p ...) carry the Biemont et al. 1998 reference and are partly Ritz-formula predictions - see conflicts. Every lifetime, hyperfine constant and frequency carries the isotope it was measured in: Stony Brook MOT work is 210Fr (I=6), ISOLDE work mostly 212Fr (I=5) and 221Fr (I=5/2), TRIUMF 206-213 and 221. measured_energy_cm (extra field on levels) holds level energies above 7S measured in a given isotope (hyperfine centres of gravity as tabulated). rme_J_ea0 is |<J||D||J'>| in e a0 in the symmetric convention of the Safronova papers / UDel portal (A = 2.02613e18 |d|^2 / ((2J'+1) lambda^3[Angstrom])). The UDel portal does carry neutral Fr (element key "Fr1": 512 distinct matrix elements, 383 rates, lifetimes for 7p-14p, 8s-14s, 6d-13d, 7 hyperfine constants; data service https://atom.ece.udel.edu/graphql behind https://www1.udel.edu/atom/); only the 7s-7p matrix elements and 7p lifetimes there are experimental (Simsarian et al. 1998), everything else is all-order theory and is marked "theory". Portal A_s / branching were computed by the portal with NIST energies, so rates into or out of 8s, 9p, 10p inherit the NIST energy errors listed under conflicts (small effect, below 0.2 % in omega^3). Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). The 7S-8S and 7S-9S entries are two-photon lines added for their measured frequencies; type "M1" marks them as E1-forbidden. Extra fields beyond the schema: ionization_energy, measured_energy_cm, unc_syst, wavenumber_cm inside frequency entries, half_life_min / mu in isotopes (abundance_percent is null: no stable isotope).
